steps.agent_response:
Yes — I can help. First, quick confirmation: event is Thursday, September 9 at 12:00 PM in the conference room with new client Ms. Samantha Lee. Before I proceed, do you know the expected headcount and any budget or cuisine preferences? If not, I can include those as questions in the messages below.

Options I can do for you:
- A) Draft/send an email to a caterer requesting menus & a quote.  
- B) Draft/send a short note to Ms. Samantha Lee asking about dietary restrictions and confirming the time/place.  
- C) Draft/send a note to your office admin or assistant asking for room setup, tableware, and cleanup.  
- D) Create all three drafts and save them to Drafts for your review.  
- E) Just give you a checklist and suggested menu options so you can decide.

Below are ready-to-use templates. Tell me which ones you want sent or drafted (and provide recipient emails or say “use address in my inbox”) and give headcount/budget/preferences if you have them.

1) To caterer — request quote and menu options
Subject: Catering request — Team lunch, Thu Sep 9 at 12:00 PM (Conference Room)
Body:
Hello [Caterer name],
We’re planning a team lunch with a client on Thursday, September 9 at 12:00 PM in our conference room and would like a catering quote and menu options. Event details:
- Date/time: Thu, Sep 9 — 12:00 PM
- Location: [Your company — Conference Room]
- Estimated guests: [insert headcount]
- Service style desired: plated / buffet / boxed lunches / family-style (please recommend)
- Dietary needs: please include vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, and nut-free options
- Setup/arrival time: please deliver and set up by 11:45 AM
- Tableware: please include disposable plates/cutlery/napkins, or note if you provide reusable
- Budget target per person: [insert budget] (optional)
Please send sample menus (2–3 options), pricing per person, staffing fees (if any), and confirmation of ability to handle dietary restrictions. We’d like to confirm by [insert decision deadline].
Thank you — please reply or call me at [your phone number] if you need details.
Best,
[Your name / team]

2) To Ms. Samantha Lee — confirm and ask dietary restrictions
Subject: Quick question — Lunch on Thu Sep 9 at 12:00 PM
Body:
Hi Ms. Lee —
I’m looking forward to our team lunch on Thursday, September 9 at 12:00 PM in our conference room. Could you please let me know if you have any dietary restrictions or preferences we should accommodate?
Also, please tell me if you’ll be bringing any guests.
Thanks — looking forward to meeting you.
Best,
[Your name]

3) To office admin / assistant — room setup & cleanup
Subject: Room setup & catering support — Thu Sep 9, 12:00 PM
Body:
Hi [Name],
We have a team lunch with a client on Thu, Sep 9 at 12:00 PM in the conference room. Can you please arrange the following?
- Setup: buffet/service table and seating for approx. [headcount]
- Tableware: plates, napkins, cutlery, serving utensils (or confirm caterer will provide)
- Trash/recycling bins placed nearby; post-event cleanup
- AV: microphone/TV as needed (if any presentations)
- Access for caterer to deliver by 11:45 AM and a contact/entry code if required
Please confirm and let me know if there are any issues.
Thanks,
[Your name]

Checklist to finalize before sending:
- Confirm final headcount
- Decide service style (buffet/plated/boxed)
- Set budget per person
- Collect dietary restrictions (ask Ms. Lee + team)
- Choose caterer or request 2–3 quotes
- Confirm delivery/setup time and who will meet the caterer
- Tableware, cutlery, napkins, trash/cleanup
- Billing details (company PO or invoice recipient)
- Decision deadline to lock menu

Next step — tell me:
- Which template(s) you want me to draft or send (A/B/C/D/E), and
- Recipient emails (caterer, Ms. Lee, office admin) or say “use address in my inbox,” plus headcount and budget (if known).

I can draft them to Drafts or send immediately once you give the recipients.

Yes — I can help coordinate. Quick confirmation: planned date/time is Thursday, September 9 at 3:00 PM with department heads Sarah, John, and Rachel. Before I proceed, tell me which of the actions below you want and any details requested.

Actions I can do for you
1) Draft invitation emails to Sarah/John/Rachel (saved in Drafts) asking them to confirm availability and preferences.

- Breakout brainstorming + creative challenge — builds collaboration and produces ideas.  
- Speed “show & tell” + micro-reflection — quick, personal, good for morale.

[Your name]

- Platform: Zoom (link below)  
- Agenda: 3:00–3:10 Icebreaker; 3:10–3:50 [Activity name]; 3:50–4:00 Debrief & next steps

Thanks,  
[Your name]

- 3:00–3:10 — Welcome & icebreaker (fun question)  
- 3:10–3:50 — Main activity (e.g., breakout teams solve challenge / trivia)  
- 3:50–4:00 — Group debrief & quick takeaways

Next step — tell me:
- Which action(s) you want (pick number(s) from Actions I can do).  
- Platform, duration, facilitator preference, budget (optional).  
- Provide participant emails or say “use addresses in my inbox” if you want me to send now.
